title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Location Encoding Methods for Species Distribution Modelling
abstract: arXiv:2611.24622v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Understanding the spatial distribution of species is a key question in ecology. A variety of solutions, from statistical, traditional machine learning, through to deep learning-based methods have been proposed. These methods take sparse observations for a species of interest as input and aim to generate dense spatial outputs indicating the spatial range of the species. Orthogonal to the choice of statistical model used is the question of what input features are most informative. Thanks to recent developments, the number of options has greatly expanded, with choices spanning different climate variables, learning-based encodings, earth embedding models, or raw transformed geographic coordinates. In this work, we introduce a standardized evaluation framework and quantify the effectiveness of different location encodings in the context of species range estimation, both at the local and global scale.

translated_title: 评估位置编码方法在物种分布建模中的有效性
translated_abstract: 理解物种的空间分布是生态学中的一个关键问题。目前已提出多种解决方案，涵盖统计方法、传统机器学习方法以及基于深度学习的方法。这些方法以目标物种的稀疏观测数据作为输入，旨在生成指示物种空间分布范围的密集空间输出。与统计模型的选择相互独立的另一个问题是：什么样的输入特征最具信息量。得益于近期的发展，可选方案的数量已大大扩展，涵盖不同的气候变量、基于学习的编码、地球嵌入模型或原始变换的地理坐标。在本工作中，我们引入了一个标准化评估框架，并在局部和全球尺度上量化了不同位置编码方法在物种分布范围估计中的有效性。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个标准化评估框架，首次系统量化了不同位置编码方法（如气候变量、学习式编码、地球嵌入模型等）在局部和全球尺度物种分布范围估计中的有效性。
